chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about selling yarn for woven clothes, where the yarn weighs more than the clothes. He said, 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell yarn for woven clothes if the yarn weighs more than the finished garment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the exchange of heavier yarn for lighter woven garments, illustrating the Shia juristic principle that value in such transactions is derived from the transformation (processing) rather than mere weight equivalence. This ruling highlights the distinction between *bay' al-gharar* (uncertainty) and legitimate trade where the added labor and material change justify the discrepancy in mass, a key concept in *al-Tahdhib*’s treatment of commercial contracts.
